clue.text: Bound to have money running short with little work

indicators.note: running short means the word for money loses its final letter

parts.note: lolly is British slang for money
op is the short form of opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone is tied to having too little cash for the small job they do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'obliged', but it is a verb meaning leap, the definition. LOLLY loses Y to give LOLL.
explanation.definitionFit: To lollop is to move along in clumsy bounds, like a rabbit or a big dog.

clue.text: How like Sibyl, to upset our Clara

indicators.note: upset means the letters of our Clara are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks how one woman resembles a prophetess, in order to annoy another.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sibyls were prophetesses of the ancient world, so to be like one is to speak in the manner of an oracle.
explanation.definitionFit: Oracular describes speech like an oracle's, prophetic and enigmatic, as the Sibyl's was.

clue.text: Loveless hooligan — he managed to become a church member

indicators.note: Loveless means the letter that stands for love, a zero score in tennis, is dropped

parts.note: a lout is a hooligan
ran, as in ran a business, means managed

explanation.surface: A thug without love somehow reformed into a churchgoer.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is O, nil in tennis scoring; 'Loveless' takes it from LOUT to leave LUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the Protestant church founded on Martin Luther's teaching is a member of that denomination.

clue.text: Bumpkins joke when lady's front pops out

indicators.note: pops out means a letter leaves the word for joke

parts.note: a pleasantry is a light joke or quip

indicators.note: the front of the word lady's is its first letter

explanation.surface: Country yokels make a jest when a woman's bodice gives way.
explanation.walkthrough: L, the front of 'lady's', leaves PLEASANTRY to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The peasantry is the class of rural farm workers, whom townsfolk mockingly call bumpkins.

clue.text: Gossip gets about after pound is taken by holy woman

indicators.note: after places the letter for about at the end, behind the other pieces

parts.note: quid is British slang for a pound sterling
a nun is a woman in a religious order
c, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A busybody goes round once the money is handed over to a nun.
explanation.definitionFit: A quidnunc is an inquisitive busybody always after the latest news, a rumour-monger.

clue.text: Important woman who came to learn from 'wise man's team

definitions.text: Important woman who came to learn from 'wise man

explanation.surface: A notable lady visited a sage, along with his followers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bible's Queen of Sheba, called the Queen of the South in the Gospels, came to hear Solomon's wisdom; the same name belongs to a Scottish football club from Dumfries.
explanation.definitionFit: Christ refers to the Queen of Sheba by this title; it is also the name of a Dumfries football team.

clue.text: Old garment that would be seen in battle

definitions.text: that would be seen in battle

explanation.surface: An ancient piece of clothing that soldiers wore into combat.
explanation.walkthrough: A doublet is also a pair of the same letter, and the word battle contains TT; the surface makes it sound like armour.
explanation.definitionFit: A doublet was a close-fitting jacket worn by men in Tudor times; it also names a pair of matching letters.

clue.text: Improper word aunt comes out with

indicators.note: comes out suggests the letters of word aunt emerge in a changed arrangement

explanation.surface: An aunt says something rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Untoward means unseemly or inappropriate, a close synonym of improper.

clue.text: Nasty old woman protecting diamonds is the official guide

indicators.note: protecting means the word for an old woman wraps around and shields another piece

parts.note: a crone is an ugly or malevolent old woman
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A spiteful old lady guarding her jewels turns out to be the tour leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nasty' is part of the old-woman phrase, not an anagram signal; 'diamonds' is underworld slang, not the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A cicerone is a guide who shows sightseers around and explains antiquities, named after the orator Cicero.

clue.text: Position of fencing to imprison witch in old city

indicators.note: to imprison means the fencing word encloses the word for a witch

parts.note: carte is a parrying position in fencing, also called quarte
a hag is a witch or ugly old woman

explanation.surface: A guard post is set up to jail a sorceress in an ancient town.
explanation.definitionFit: Carthage was the ancient Phoenician city in North Africa, destroyed by Rome.

clue.text: Country game with short piece of wood

parts.note: RU is short for rugby union, the game

indicators.note: short means the word for a piece of wood loses its last letter

parts.note: a stick is a piece of wood

explanation.surface: A rural sport played with a little wooden bat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' is an adjective here, as in country life; STICK cut short gives STIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustic means rural, belonging to the countryside.

clue.text: Lord, there's all but nothing tiptop in a tabloid!

indicators.note: in means the pieces before it sit inside the word for a tabloid

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

indicators.note: all but means the word for nothing loses its final letter

parts.note: zero means nothing
A1 means first-rate, written AI in crossword letters

explanation.surface: A peer is upset to find himself treated as a nobody in a top red-top.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark hints at the tabloid's taste for headlines; A1 is read as the letters AI, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A suzerain is a feudal overlord or sovereign with power over a vassal state.

clue.text: Look angry, given a shiner?

explanation.surface: Someone scowls after being punched in the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: A shiner suggests a black eye, but read it as something that shines: one that glows.
explanation.definitionFit: To glower is to scowl angrily; read playfully, a glow-er is something that glows, a shiner.

clue.text: Manufactured product with processed fat (trace)

indicators.note: processed suggests the letters of fat and trace are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A factory item contains a bit of processed fat.
explanation.definitionFit: An artefact is an object made by human hands, a man-made item.

clue.text: Chatted in study, sitting on amazing piece of furniture

indicators.note: in a down clue sitting on places the word for study above the following pieces

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
fab, short for fabulous, means amazing
a bed is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: People talked in a den while perched on a fabulous sofa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'study' is a verb here, not a room.
explanation.definitionFit: To confab, short for confabulate, is to chat informally.

clue.text: Bird, one leaving evidence all around London monument

definitions.text: one leaving evidence all around London monument

explanation.surface: A bird that has left its droppings all over a famous London landmark.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Christopher Wren designed St Paul's and dozens of London churches; his epitaph says that if you seek his monument, look around.
explanation.definitionFit: The wren is a small songbird; Christopher Wren left his works all over London as his memorial.

clue.text: Museum needs to increase in size when given all author's books

parts.note: to wax is to grow, as the moon does
an author's works are all the books written

explanation.surface: A library must expand when donated a writer's entire output.
explanation.definitionFit: A waxworks is a museum displaying wax figures of famous people.

clue.text: Conclusion briefly practicable is much to be desired

indicators.note: briefly means the word for conclusion is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: an end is a conclusion
viable means practicable or workable

explanation.surface: A neat, workable ending is what everyone wants.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enviable is so good that others covet it, highly desirable.

clue.text: Something with sharp edge carried by mad zealot

indicators.note: carried by means the letters are held inside the words mad zealot

explanation.surface: A fanatic is brandishing a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: An adze is a cutting tool with an arched blade set at right angles to its handle.

clue.text: A person with records and excellent set of books alongside

parts.note: a DJ, disc jockey, plays records
ace means excellent
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A record collector with a fine library sits nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjacent means next to or lying beside something.

clue.text: Australia upset over country's division into different areas

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the first piece above the next
in a down clue upset turns the word for Australia upside down, reading backwards

parts.note: Oz is a nickname for Australia
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: Australians are angry about the partition of their land.
explanation.definitionFit: Zonation is the arrangement or division of something into distinct zones.

clue.text: Joined as torch-bearer

explanation.surface: Someone signed up to carry the Olympic flame.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: the word torch-bearer is written with a hyphen.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyphened means joined with a hyphen, as the two halves of torch-bearer are.

clue.text: Workers at university given order to surrender

parts.note: hands are manual workers, as on a farm
up means at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: Staff at a college are told to give themselves up.
explanation.definitionFit: Hands up is the command to raise your arms in surrender.

clue.text: Beastly sound — reason for staying outside pub

indicators.note: staying outside means the word for reason sits around the word for pub

parts.note: why means reason, as in the why and wherefore
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: An animal noise explains why someone loiters outside a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A whinny is the gentle neigh of a horse, an animal's sound.

clue.text: Stolen goods taken round American state by a rascal

indicators.note: taken round means the word for loot goes around the other pieces

parts.note: swag is a thief's loot
Cal is an abbreviation of California

explanation.surface: A rogue carries loot across a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalawag, or scallywag, is a mischievous rogue.

clue.text: Strong bull squashing vehicle

indicators.note: squashing means the word for bull presses around the vehicle

parts.note: bull is slang for nonsense, as is rot
a bus is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A powerful bull crushes a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bull' is not the animal but nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Robust means sturdy and strong.

clue.text: Pub Emile renovated, providing cheap food once

indicators.note: renovated suggests the letters of Pub Emile are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Emile's refurbished tavern serves a low-cost menu.
explanation.definitionFit: Umble pie was a pie of deer offal, food for servants, now remembered in the phrase humble pie.

clue.text: Embarrassed Dickensian clerk is restricted by demand for silence

indicators.note: restricted by means the clerk and is are held within the call for quiet

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
Uriah Heep is the scheming clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield

explanation.surface: A Dickens clerk is shamed after being hushed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheepish means awkwardly embarrassed or shamefaced.

clue.text: Fond pet hovering around source of food?

indicators.note: hovering around means the word for pet stays about the source of food

parts.note: a dog is a household pet
a tin, a can, is a source of food

explanation.surface: A pet hangs round where its dinner comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Doting means extravagantly fond or loving.
